C08-M07-L05-F1.title: Diagnosing a noisy rule before choosing the change
C08-M07-L05-F1.caption: Four questions, asked in order, lead from a measured precision problem to the most general durable fix, and every fix passes the same gate.
C08-M07-L05-F1.alt: Decision graph, top to bottom. A slate box, Noisy rule (measured precision and volume), leads to a violet decision: Is the data wrong? Yes leads to Fix parser or normalisation; no leads to the next decision: Logic broader than intent? Yes leads to Narrow the logic; no leads to: Threshold or window off baseline? Yes leads to Re-set from measured baseline; no leads to: Known authorised instance? Yes leads to Scoped suppression (owner, reason, expiry); no leads to Lower priority, keep visible. All five outcome boxes lead to one dark box: Tests, replay and review.
C08-M07-L05-F1.note: Stop at the first yes: the higher the fix, the wider and more durable its effect.

C08-M07-L05-F2.title: Change control for a detection rule
C08-M07-L05-F2.caption: The controlled path from a tuning request to a monitored production rule, with tests and replay as the evidence gates.
C08-M07-L05-F2.alt: Flow diagram, top to bottom, eight steps: Tuning request (precision, volume, FP records); Reproduce on stored data; Branch: rule + tests (commit cites the ticket); Unit tests (must-match, must-not, boundary); Replay (volume and precision over past data); Peer review and approval; Staged deployment (status test, low priority or shadow); Monitor and roll back if needed. A dashed arrow loops from the last step back to Tuning request, labelled post-deployment evidence opens the next request.

steps.label: Replay
steps.sub: volume and precision over past data

steps.label: Staged deployment
steps.sub: status test, low priority or shadow

steps.label: Monitor and roll back if needed

loop.label: post-deployment evidence opens the next request

C08-M07-L05-F2.note: A failing test or a replay that loses a true positive sends the change back, never forward.
